original_contract.question: For a finite-dimensional representation (phi, V) of a group G, the dual representation (phi^*, V^*) is defined by phi^*(g)(L) = L . phi(g)^{-1}. (a) Prove that in a basis phi^*(g) = phi(g^{-1})^T, and that if (phi, V) is unitary then phi^*(g) = conj(phi(g)) (the entrywise complex conjugate). (b) Delineate the boundary between a representation and its dual: give the character relation chi_{V^*}(g) = conj(chi_V(g)) for unitary representations, and explain precisely when V is isomorphic to its dual (self-dual) versus not, giving an explicit example of a NON-self-dual irreducible representation. (c) State what remains true regardless: (phi^*, V^*) is irreducible iff (phi, V) is.

With C2 generator D=diag(1,-1) and P=[[1,1],[0,1]], M=P^-1DP=[[1,2],[0,-1]] while M^-T=[[1,0],[2,-1]], so conjugate(M) is not the dual matrix.
